newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation on tobacco deal seen.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation on tobacco deal seen.

text.p: As negotiators for states and the tobacco industry tried to hammer out a settlement of lawsuits against the industry, investors continued to use options, particularly in Philip Morris Cos Inc, to speculate on a deal, options traders said Thursday.
In afternoon activity, Philip Morris options were the most active group at the American Stock Exchange, led by the January 1999 46-5/8 call, which traded 7,780 contracts.
The June 50 was next in line, with volume of 7,360 contracts, followed by the June 45 calls, with nearly 5,735.
The July 50 call and September 50 call also were busy. On the put side, the June 46-5/8s traded 2,125 contracts.
One options trader said he had customers coming in to buy the June 50 calls, even though they were still more than two points out of the money and expire at the end of the week.
In consolidated afternoon trading, Philip Morris shares were up 2-1/8 at 47-5/8 on more than 12.6 million shares.
"We've got some speculators coming in," the options trader said, adding that other investors were rolling long positions into the July series.

Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said some investors were probably closing out their June 50 call positions. The option was up 3/16 at 1/4 and had open interest of about 17,050 contracts.

"There's no sense in rolling that (position) so it could be just an outright close," he said. "That volume could be (investors) not taking the chance of losing the stock from news that may come out after 4 o'clock (1600 EDT/2000 GMT) today or tomorrow."
The stock market closes at 1600 EDT/2000 GMT.
Some tobacco negotiators said Thursday they were optimistic an agreement would be reached soon.
Sources close to both the state attorneys general and the tobacco industry said they doubted a deal would be reached until late Thursday at the earliest.
June options stop trading Friday and technically expire Saturday and Schwartz noted that holders of those options have until 1730 EDT/2130 GMT Friday to exercise.
"Will these people be rewarded? You can be certain they'll be sittting at their TV sets until 5:30 (1730 EDT/2130 GMT) on Friday, which is exercise cutoff time," he said.
"Brokers who have positions for customers will be staying late Friday night," Schwartz predicted.
He added that it appeared investors were rolling positions mainly into the July and September 50 calls and that the January 1999 46-5/8 call volume was most likely from investors opening positions.
One options dealer in Chicago said volatilities in the Philip Morris June and July options were up slightly Thursday.
